invariant: Every array subquery in a structured result MAY specify a finite child `limit` (zero is valid); omission selects the complete ordered suffix after `offset`. Logical result size MUST NOT be constrained by a transport frame limit: transport decomposition and reassembly MUST preserve the complete logical message atomically.

`FilterOp` MUST emit exactly the input deltas whose records satisfy its `PredicateExpr`, preserving record bytes and weights, for the supported predicate surface including `And`/`Or`, literal comparisons, field-to-field equality/inequality, and `Contains`/`ContainsField`.
`BindingId` MUST be derived from canonical binding bytes in parameter-name order, and bindings MUST reject missing, unknown, or type-mismatched params.

An aggregate result member's identity MUST be derived structurally from its group key, and a scalar global aggregate MUST lower to one fixed synthetic identity. Neither the identity nor any delivery decision keyed on it may be derived from, or matched against, a constructed name such as `<table>_aggregate`; filtering delivery by string comparison against a table name is forbidden.

Aggregate output types are fixed by function: `count` is `U64` and never null; `sum`, `min`, `max` are nullable over the non-nullable base type of their input; `avg` is `Nullable(F64)` and stays finite for large finite inputs. Integer and bigint aggregates keep signed public values.

A stored SQL NULL and an omitted value MUST stay distinguishable until the public boundary: an explicit null is kept over a column default, an omitted optional column reads as null, and a non-null value in a nullable column reads back as itself.

A group present with a NULL aggregate, an absent group, and a group whose aggregate value changed are three distinct outcomes the delivered result MUST distinguish. An empty group and an all-NULL group are both present-with-NULL, not absent.

The non-aggregate fields of a synthetic aggregate row — row id, version, provenance, deletion state — carry no meaning. Producers MUST NOT populate them with interpretable values and consumers MUST NOT read them.
A delivered change for an aggregate member the subscriber does not hold MUST arrive as an add, not an update: a grouped member that leaves and returns is added again.

Rows, history and pending uploads MUST persist in the SQLite file; subscriptions, settlement waits and per-peer delivery state are process-local and are rebuilt after reopen. A reopened replica answers local-first reads from its file and re-sends its pending uploads; a fresh remote read needs a new answer from upstream.

A keyed `Lookup` MUST output exactly the rows of its table, under its static prefix, whose primary-key columns after that prefix equal a key with positive multiplicity in its input, each row once however often its key occurs, and MUST keep that relation maintained as keys enter or leave and as matched rows are inserted, updated or deleted.

A keyed `Lookup` MUST read storage only by key: one prefix read per distinct live key at hydration and per entering key at a tick, never the rows of keys that are not live, so its work is bounded by its keys and the changes touching them, not by the table's size.

Recursive reads (gather queries, recursive relations, recursive policies) MUST use set semantics, so they reach a fixpoint on cyclic edges, include their seed, and stop at a declared depth bound; a cycle in an inherited policy denies only the rows it reaches. (Folds groove INV-REC-3, INV-REC-6, INV-REC-17.)
SQL predicate lowering MUST reject unsupported or ill-typed predicate expressions instead of lowering them approximately.
Shape registration MUST reject an AST whose content-addressed id does not match `shape_id`, and MUST park registrations naming an unknown schema version until the schema catalogue arrives.
A one-shot read MUST be served once without installing live delivery, and MUST NOT change what any open subscription receives. (Folds groove INV-OK-3, INV-TICK-19.)

A subscription delivery MUST contain only changes to that subscription's result: a write to a row outside the result delivers nothing, and a change to an included row updates only the members that include it. (Folds groove INV-TICK-3, INV-QUERY-28.)
`MapProjectOp` MUST emit one output delta per input delta, copying only configured fields into the output descriptor and preserving the input weight.

A `Subscribe` MUST carry its whole compiled query and bindings, keyed by a subscription id the subscriber chooses; `Unsubscribe` MUST end that subscription's delivery and forget its result, and a later subscribe of the same query starts clean.
`UnwrapNullableOp` MUST drop `Nullable(None)` input deltas, unwrap `Nullable(Some(_))` to the inner value, and preserve the original delta weight.

On `Subscribe` the serving side MUST run the query for the subscriber's identity and answer with its full current result before any change, so a fresh subscription's first delivery is its whole opening (possibly empty, once settled).
`Union` MUST require all non-empty inputs to have the same output descriptor and MUST preserve duplicate derivations as separate weighted deltas (`UNION ALL` semantics).
A reset delivery MUST replace the subscriber's whole result for that subscription (members it no longer lists leave) while keeping the order and update category of members that stay.
An inner `JoinOp` MUST require equal-length left and right key vectors.

Live result members MUST be addressed by row id (a flat join by its contributing row ids, a history read by row id and seq) and carry the version they show, so a new version of a member is delivered even when its projected cells are unchanged.
An inner JoinOp MUST emit joined records with weight leftweight \* rightweight for matching keys, including matches produced by changes arriving on either side.

A synced result MUST ship the rows the reader may read that the query outputs or reads (include targets, array children, join and gather edges); rows the query traverses but does not keep, and rows the reader may not read, MUST NOT be shipped.

Opening a serializable transaction MUST fix its snapshot at the newest commit seq this node holds (plus its own unsettled writes); a read the snapshot cannot answer locally waits for the authority rather than reading a later state.
A delete MUST hide the row and its history from ordinary reads, an update to a deleted row MUST be refused rather than restoring it, and only an explicit restore reveals its current content again.
A LocalFirst read on the writer MUST include its own pending writes at once, while a Remote read MUST withhold them until the authority has accepted and settled them.
Each current table MUST hold, per (id, branch key), the newest accepted version, and its history table every accepted version; both MUST agree after reopen.

A snapshot MUST cover exactly the versions at or below its commit seq plus the unsettled writes it names; a snapshot captured offline names its unsettled writes and keeps them after they settle, an online capture waits for them to settle.
Reads inside an open serializable transaction MUST see each row as of the snapshot (from history when it changed since) and MUST NOT observe later writes.
Reads inside an open transaction MUST overlay that transaction's own staged writes on top of its base view.
A serializable read MUST be recorded whether it found rows or not, so an absent row that appears before commit conflicts as surely as a present row that changes.

`tx_current_rows` and `tx_query` MUST record predicate reads as `PredicateRead` values carrying `table`, `shape_id`, `shape`, `binding_id`, and `binding_values`; whole-table transaction reads are degenerate query shapes.

A node's current row MUST be the authority image with the highest seq it holds for that row, with the node's pending overlay on top for local reads; receiving images of a row out of seq order MUST leave the same current row as receiving them in order.
Current-row reads MUST leave out deleted rows unless the query asks for deleted rows; then deleted rows read with their deletion metadata and stay under the read policy.
As-of reads at a commit seq MUST read each row's newest version at or before that seq from history, and leave out rows deleted as of it.
A recursive graph MUST have a seed child and a step child whose output `RecordDescriptor`s are identical; otherwise subscription/compilation MUST fail with `GraphOutputMismatch`.

Context-dependent recursive arrangements MUST be keyed by `ScopePath` and recursive `sub_tick`; root-scope arrangements MUST use `sub_tick = 0` and MUST absorb a public tick's table delta exactly once even when recursive and non-recursive consumers share them.
Hydrating a new subscriber to an already-shared recursive node MUST return the full current recursive result and MUST NOT consume or suppress future tick deltas for existing subscribers.
Recursive recompute MUST NOT persist per-context child operator state in the runtime state maps after recompute completes.

Jazz MUST reject user-authored logical operations that would lower to `arg_max_by` or `arg_min_by` inside a recursive seed or step before resolving physical current-row sources. Physical ArgBy introduced by that source expansion MAY occur inside recursion and MUST use the same declared-key direction and ascending full-record tie-breaker as non-recursive evaluation before its winners enter recursive set accumulation.
SQL lowering MUST either preserve a query's semantics exactly or reject it explicitly.
Nested recursive graphs MUST be rejected during validation/compilation.
A terminal collector's touched-rendered-group bound MUST NOT be applied to recursive fixed-point state, iterations, or nested logical time.

Semantically depth-bounded recursion MUST include the depth-zero seed and facts produced by at most `max_iters` step evaluations, including no step frontier when `max_iters = 0`, and discard the next frontier without reporting non-convergence; maintained base or binding changes MUST preserve that seed-relative depth.

`FrontierSourceOp` MUST read only the `RecordDeltas` bound for its `FrontierName` in the current `EvalContext`; when absent it MUST yield an empty weighted record set with the declared output descriptor.
Recursive facts MUST use set semantics: an encoded fact already present in `RecursiveState::accumulated` MUST NOT be emitted again or have its weight increased by duplicate derivations.
Accepted recursive facts MUST be emitted with weight `1`; positive recursive deltas with weight greater than one MUST collapse to one accepted fact.
Positive-only recursive evaluation MUST reject any non-positive frontier delta with `IvmRuntimeError::UnsupportedNonMonotoneRecursion`.
A recursive fixpoint MUST stop when the accepted frontier is empty and MUST converge on cyclic inputs by deduplicating against accumulated facts.
Fixpoint recursion MUST fail with `IvmRuntimeError::RecursiveIterationLimit { node, max_iters }` when the number of step iterations exceeds its independent safety limit.
Retractions reaching recursive state MUST be handled by full recompute from storage and diff against the previous accumulated set; subscribers MUST receive only the resulting net recursive delta.
After recompute, recursive step arrangements MUST be hydrated from full table snapshots and the full accumulated weighted record set before future positive incremental use.

A read MUST compose its layers by one rule: the top layer holding a row supplies it, live or deleted, and masks the layers below before any predicate or relational operator applies. A replica's pending writes are the top layer over its settled rows; a branch view's head is the top layer over its base.

A read's layers MUST follow its tier: a `Remote` read is the authority's result alone, without pending local writes; `LocalFirst` and `LocalOnly` read the replica's pending writes over its settled rows.
An indexed branch-view read MUST give the same rows as the unindexed read: the head masks the base under the index, and changes on either branch reach an indexed subscription.

Whether a write chains on its writer's own unsettled write MUST NOT be encoded in stored or sent bytes: a commit carries only its operations, and the writer's replica rebases its remaining pending commits over each settled image it receives.

A replica MUST keep a row's settled image while a pending local commit overrides it (`_jazz_shadow`), update that image from server images, and on a settle or rejection rebase: restore every shadowed row and replay the remaining pending commits in order. Shadows and pending commits survive a restart.

A commit from a session MUST be refused whole, with an authorization-denied rejection and none of its rows applied, when any of its writes fails its table's write policy for the identity it is checked as. The author recorded as provenance differs from that identity only through a trusted serving link (INV-RLS-17, INV-RLS-18).

A synced query MUST be served with the root table's read policy compiled into it and its session values bound from the server-authenticated identity, so a client cannot widen what it sees through parameters; each identity's binding is routed separately.
Relay peer links MUST have an explicit relay transport capability and no permission subject; client-to-Core peer links MUST use the admitted client `AuthorSubject` for policy-composed reads.
implementation: planned explicit relay transport capability and permission-subject separation

invariant: The rows a serializable commit writes MUST reach each subscriber in one delivery and filtered by that subscriber's read policy: a reader never sees part of the commit, nor rows of it it may not read.
coverage: partial: per-reader filtering of a serializable commit has no dedicated test

invariant: History and as-of reads MUST be gated by the read policy of the row as it is now: a reader sees a row's versions only while it may read the current row, and loses them when that access goes.
Policy evaluation MUST deny when it cannot establish that a policy holds: a missing or deleted inherited parent, a cycle, an absent claim or a NULL comparison all deny.

Every table policy set is closed: an operation (read, insert, update, delete) without a declared policy MUST deny it to every non-system identity, and a declared update MAY omit its old-row or new-row clause. An anonymous identity reads and writes only what policies grant its auth mode.

A write whose recorded author differs from the identity it is checked as MUST come through a trusted serving link (a backend acting for a session, or attributing to a user); the write policy is evaluated for the identity the link vouches for, while the author stays provenance.

An uploaded commit MUST be authorized under its link's authenticated identity: on a session link a different author is refused (attribution requires a trusted serving node) and the write is checked as the link, while a trusted link may attribute and have the write checked as the session it acts for.

A required relation MUST count as resolved for a non-system reader only through rows the reader may read: a parent whose required related rows are missing or unreadable is left out, so the relation cannot reveal rows the reader may not see.
The system identity (the database's own writes, an admin-secret link) MUST bypass read and write policies; every other identity is checked.

A session's update, patch, upsert over an existing row, or transactional write MUST also satisfy the target row's read policy; a hidden target fails without disclosing its cells, existence or policy, and an upsert applies the insert policy only when the target is truly absent.

A read or write policy subplan MUST read every table source it evaluates as raw policy evidence without recursively applying that source table's own read policy. The complete evaluating policy—including filters, joins, authenticated claims, policy branches, inheritance, and reachability—MUST still be enforced fail-closed, and dependency rows MUST NOT thereby become user-visible.

Client mutation staging MUST NOT issue a definitive read- or write-policy verdict from partial local state. Update/upsert read visibility and write policy are enforced by the fate authority against its complete admitted policy inputs.
implementation: planned removal of client-local transaction policy preflight

invariant: External JWT application metadata MUST use the flat JWT payload: every non-registered top-level claim is exposed at `session.claims[<name>]`; `iss`, `sub`, `aud`, `exp`, `nbf`, `iat`, and `jti` are reserved transport/security claims; and Jazz MUST NOT specially interpret a nested `claims` object.

A row the server evicts as unreadable MUST leave the replica's local reads for that reader, before joins, aggregates and windows, and stay out across reopen until the server readmits it; evicting it never touches the server's own rows.

Session values a policy compares with (the user, the provider subject, other claims, the auth mode) MUST be bound from the authenticated identity and its admitted claims, never from caller-supplied query parameters.
A table policy MUST validate as a query shape rooted at the table that carries the policy.
A server MUST ship a non-system peer only rows its read policy admits, including support rows and deleted rows.

When a write takes a row out of a reader's read access, the server MUST unlist it from that reader's later settled results but MUST NOT redact the copy already delivered; when a policy change or a check of held rows finds a row unreadable, the server MUST evict it and the replica drops its copy.
A session's delete MUST satisfy the table's delete policy against the row's current version; deleting a row that is absent or already deleted MUST be refused.
A deleted row and its deletion metadata MUST be readable to a non-system identity only when the deleted row itself satisfies that identity's read policy.

An EXISTS policy MUST require at least one matching proof row for the same identity: a correlated EXISTS reaches the protected row, an uncorrelated one gates every row on the proof set being nonempty without duplicating results, and removing the last proof revokes access. Proof rows are the committed rows, plus the earlier inserts of the same commit for its WITH CHECK clauses; a new row is never evidence for itself.
Graphs containing `BindingSource` MUST NOT be evaluated through ordinary `query_snapshot`, `subscribe`, or `subscribe_query`; they MUST be evaluated only through prepared-shape APIs.
Unsubscribing a shape subscription MUST decrement the binding refcount and MUST inject a `-1` binding delta only when the last reference is removed.
Binding retractions discovered via dropped receivers during notification MUST be queued, then drained before subsequent user table/binding deltas and before prepare/bind hydration snapshots.
Preparing an identical shape over an already-active binding source MUST NOT replace shared arrangements with an empty binding snapshot or otherwise wipe existing bindings.
During shape graph hydration, `BindingSource` nodes in `ArrangementUpdateMode::Replace` MUST read current binding snapshots, not pending/incremental binding deltas.
`Database::bind` MUST accept exactly one value for each prepared parameter name, MUST reject missing/duplicate/unknown names, and MUST pass values to `bind_shape` in prepared parameter order.
Binding values MUST conform to the prepared shape's `binding_descriptor`; mismatched type/arity MUST fail before subscription hydration.
Prepared shapes MUST retain their output graph nodes while the shape remains registered.
A `BindingSource` tick in normal accumulate mode MUST emit only `BindingDelta`s whose `shape` matches the source's `BindingSourceOp.shape` and whose descriptor matches the node output.
Prepared recursive shapes MUST route retractions caused by base-table deletes or anti-join changes to the correct bound subscriber result.
`Database::prepare_query` MUST reject queries without parameters and MUST lower only equality `column = parameter` / `parameter = column` predicates into binding joins.

A prepared-query internal graph output MUST include every binding key column needed for routing, while `PreparedShape::output` and bound subscription rows MUST expose only the public query projection; projected output names that collide with parameter names MUST be rejected except for the same source field.
Graph-level `prepare` MUST reject any `output_key_fields` entry absent from the graph output descriptor.
A binding source weighted record set MUST expose set semantics: for each active `BindingKey`, evaluation snapshots contain exactly one row with weight `+1`, regardless of subscriber refcount.
Binding a key whose refcount transitions 0 -> 1 MUST inject exactly one `+1` `BindingDelta` in a table-delta-free tick before serving the subscriber snapshot.
Binding an already-active key MUST NOT inject another binding-source delta, and MUST serve the new subscriber from the per-key materialized snapshot.

Shape deltas MUST be routed by projecting the prepared output record through `output_key_fields`, or the explicit routing graph output through `routing_key_fields`, into the binding descriptor, and MUST be sent only to subscribers registered for that binding key.
A prepared binding's materialized snapshot MUST be maintained as a weighted multiset where deltas that bring a record weight to zero remove that record.

Chapter 15 MUST NOT describe sharded core as implemented; conforming current implementations MUST treat sharding as an exploratory/open design area. This is a guidance/process anchor, not runtime conformance.
A future sharded design MUST keep a global catalogue/sequencer for schema versions, lenses, policy bundles, and the partition-ownership map unless this chapter explicitly replaces that architecture.
A future sharded design MUST define settled positions as per-shard positions or vectors, and MUST specify how `at(position)` and `at_time(t)` resolve across shards.
A multi-shard subscription result MUST NOT be marked complete unless completeness evidence has been obtained for every shard contributing to the result.
Cross-shard permission closures MUST be obtained through shard-core subscriptions or an explicitly equivalent mechanism before a shard-core assigns a fate that depends on remote-shard policy data.

Rebalancing MUST NOT flip partition ownership in the catalogue until the destination shard-core has the partition history needed to serve that ownership and the protocol has defined treatment of in-flight fates/subscriptions.
A future sharded v1 MUST assign every non-global row to a schema-declared shard partition key, and MUST specify behavior for rows without a natural root and rows whose root changes.
Future v1 serializable transactions MUST be single-shard unless a cross-shard serialization mechanism is explicitly specified.
A cross-shard serializable transaction MUST NOT be accepted without validation evidence for every shard touched by its row and predicate read-sets.

`OrderedKvStorage::scan(ScanRequest)` MUST return range results in the requested lexicographic direction and include keys `>= start` while excluding keys `>= end`; when `start >= end`, it MUST return an empty result without panicking.
Fixed-width nullable nulls MUST encode as flag `0` plus zero-filled reserved payload width; variable-width nullable nulls MUST encode as only flag `0`.
Fixed-width arrays MUST encode as concatenated element encodings without an element count; variable-width arrays MUST encode `count: u32`, offsets for all but the final element, then payloads.
`F64` record and ordered-key values MUST NOT be NaN, including caller-supplied raw records at durable admission.
`ScalarEnumSchema` values MUST persist and compare by declaration-order `u8` discriminant; appending variants is compatible, but reordering/removing variants changes stored meaning.

Primary-key bytes MUST be order-preserving tagged encodings: integer payloads big-endian, `Bool` as `0|1`, `Uuid` raw bytes, and `String`/`Bytes` escaped with embedded NUL `00 ff` plus terminator `00 00`.
Table writes MUST reject rows whose primary-key values do not match the declared `PrimaryKeyColumn.key_type`, and MUST reject table writes for tables with no primary key.
Inserts MUST reject an existing primary key, including keys introduced by earlier operations in the same `DatabaseBatch`.
Base table writes MUST be staged before the tick and flushed together with durable tick writes only after the tick succeeds.
Runtime storage reads during a staged tick MUST observe staged set/delete operations before committed storage, including same-tick durable `Persist` writes.
A prefix `ScanRequest` MUST return exactly keys beginning with the supplied byte prefix in the requested lexicographic direction, including prefixes whose finite upper bound cannot be computed.

Directly exposed record stores MUST be typed record stores with record-encoded values and order-preserving typed primary keys, while bypassing table batches, primary-key table scans, durable index maintenance, query planning, and IVM ticks. A single trailing variable-width `Bytes` value column MUST encode as exactly the stored bytes.
`DatabaseSchema::column_families()` MUST include the `"indices"` column family whenever any table declares an `IndexSchema`, and MUST omit it when no schema index exists.

A durable index entry key MUST be the minimal LEB128 durable index id (never 0) followed by the concatenated `encode_key_part` index-column parts with no second escaping or wrapper. A non-unique index whose columns do not cover the primary key MUST append a `0xff` separator and the encoded primary-key columns the index lacks; a unique or primary-key-covering index MUST omit that suffix. The value MUST be empty, except that a unique index not covering the primary key stores exactly the encoded primary-key columns the index lacks.

Durable unique-index ownership MUST be resolved from the consolidated final deltas of one storage-atomic batch. A different record may replace the durable owner only when that batch fully retracts the old owner and leaves at most one positive owner; competing positive owners MUST be rejected.

Persisted index scans MUST rebuild the primary key from the decoded index-column parts plus the entry's `0xff` suffix (non-unique) or stored value (unique), consuming both exactly, and fetch the current base table record; a malformed entry, or a missing base record for a primary-key table, MUST make the index invalid.

Ordered index key encoding via `encode_key_part` MUST preserve logical ordering for supported key values in RocksDB lexicographic order and MUST reject arrays as keys; concatenated parts of mixed column types, including NUL/0xff bytes and variable-length strings, MUST be prefix-free and decode back exactly.
Record-store persistence is row-only: each logical stored record has its canonical row key/value entry, and no storage maintenance may replace a run of rows with a second logical representation.
A record-valued `ValueType` MUST carry its descriptor inline and its encoder MUST emit canonical child bytes; it MUST NOT appear, directly or recursively, in a durable primary key.

`put_if_absent` and `compare_and_delete` MUST be atomic at one persistence scope: a backend serializes them across concurrent handles or enforces exclusive open; comparison uses exact stored bytes so stale cleanup cannot delete a reinstalled logical value (ABA).

An explicit ordered scan request with a finite item bound MUST yield at most that many entries in its requested order, and backends MUST stop traversal/hydration at the bound rather than treating it as caller-side collection advice.

Application table and direct-record-store names MUST be unique and case-sensitive, and MUST not use `__groove_*`, `indices`, or `default`; initial and live schema admission rejects them before Groove durable mutation. Every physical backend ingress MUST reject embedded NUL and names exceeding `u16::MAX` UTF-8 bytes before durable mutation, catalogue admission, or live-memory replacement.

A durable adapter MUST validate its epoch-pinned physical manifest before mutating a pre-existing store; backend commit/WAL sync is the durability boundary, while flushes/checkpoints are maintenance; engine files are not logical interchange. The caller selects one closed, sorted opaque codec profile; omission, addition, duplication, or substitution fails admission, while adapters do not interpret higher-layer codec semantics. IndexedDB's fixed `storage-manifest`/`epoch` record pins its epoch, adapter/page format, selected codec profile, page size, and checksum parameters; its separate `replica-node-v1` record is an exact 16-byte physical-replica identity, created atomically with a fresh manifest and validated before opening Jazz.

An atomic batch acknowledgement MUST distinguish committed, definitely-uncommitted, and possibly-committed outcomes. Only a definitely-uncommitted result permits retry or runtime rollback. Cancellation before an ordered write starts may retry; cancellation after submission starts and an explicit possibly-committed result MUST poison the resident database before any retry or rollback can occur. Cancelling an in-flight publication MUST wake every later ordered waiter with the terminal order failure. The poison is instance-local: reopening observes the prior durable state, does not retry the abandoned resident publication, and permits fresh writes.

A payload `EnumValue` MUST persist its declaration-order `u32` case tag as a minimal little-endian base-128 varint immediately followed by the selected case's canonical record payload; unknown, truncated, overflowing, and non-minimal tags are invalid.

`MemoryStorage` restart snapshots MUST use only the explicit canonical V1 `GMS1` length-delimited map codec; malformed, truncated, trailing, duplicate, or alternate-order bytes MUST fail before they replace resident storage, and earlier serde/postcard snapshot bytes have no compatibility path.

Jazz's epoch-1 class-CF view MUST admit only marker key `groove-storage-layout` with value `class-cf-v3`, use the specified ordered logical-family classifier and physical class names, and frame mapped keys as the logical family's class table id (u32 big-endian, at most 2^24-1) followed by the logical key, except that the `indices` class (whose only logical family is `indices`) stores logical keys unframed. The id is derived from the family name alone: a per-table family `jazz_physical_{id}_{history|global_current|ahead_current|rejected_versions}` carries its catalogue physical table id (at most 2^24-257), each fixed Jazz system family has a static id above that range, and an operation on any other mapped family fails closed before storage access. Missing, malformed, old (`class-cf-v1`, `class-cf-v2`), or future markers in a nonempty mapped/class store fail closed before logical access; no legacy migration or fallback exists within epoch 1.

A declared-index generation repair MUST preserve all primary and non-index storage bytes, make the declared indexes' id registrations durable before any rebuilt entry, clear and rebuild only declared index prefixes before index-dependent recovery, and durably publish completion only after all rebuilt indexes are durable; interrupted incomplete repair MUST retry on reopen and a matching generation MUST skip repair.

A `U48` value MUST lie in `0..=2^48-1` and MUST be rejected on encode otherwise. It is constant-width: exactly 6 bytes little-endian as a record scalar in the fixed-width region, exactly 6 bytes big-endian as a fixed tuple member, `Nullable<U48>` is a flag plus a 6-byte zero-when-null payload, primary-key and ordered-index parts are tag `0x10` plus 6 big-endian bytes, and the persisted descriptor node tag is 25.

Durable index ids MUST be assigned per `(table, index, definition)` from a monotonic counter starting at 1, recorded in the `indices` registry (`\0groove-index-id\0` keys) no later than the storage-atomic write of the first entry that uses them, stable across reopen and index reordering, and never reused: a changed definition or a runtime (re)registration receives a fresh id, so entries of an earlier incarnation are never read. An `indices` family holding entries without the `groove-durable-index-v2` layout marker, or with another marker, MUST fail open with `InvalidStorageLayout`; node roots declare `groove.durable-index.v2` in their manifest.
`write_many` MUST apply all `Set`/`Delete` operations atomically at the storage-operation level, and a missing column family in the operation list MUST leave earlier valid operations unapplied.
`ReopenableStorage::reopen` MUST preserve existing data while adding newly requested column families.
Table records MUST be stored as values in the table column family named by `TableSchema::name`, keyed by the encoded primary key derived from the row record.
Public insert/update values MUST be interpreted in `TableSchema.columns` declaration order, independent of the `RecordDescriptor` physical encoding order.
`RecordDescriptor::fields()` and field indices MUST remain in logical declaration order even though encoded bytes may reorder fixed-width fields before variable-width fields.

Fixed-width record scalar payloads and record/array offsets MUST use little-endian encoding inside record values; fixed-width tuple members MUST use the big-endian order-preserving member encoding on encode, decode and structural validation alike, recursively through nested tuple and nullable members (a present nullable member's payload is itself a member), with `F64` members in the §2.8 ordered-index transform.

A replica MUST apply a result whole: a first result larger than one frame is split into rows messages whose last part ends it, and nothing of it is visible before the end; a commit split across frames is applied whole.
A reset after reconnect MUST replace the subscription's whole result (members no longer listed leave) while the server keeps skipping versions the peer is known to hold.
A server MUST ship other peers accepted rows only, never another node's pending or refused writes.
A server MUST apply the peer identity's read policy before shipping any row image, support row or count to it.
A write that takes away a reader's access MUST remove the row from that reader's later settled results (it is unlisted) but MUST NOT require redacting the copy already delivered.

A serializable commit MUST be decided and applied whole at the authority and reach replicas whole: no replica shows part of a serializable commit, and a commit through a relay is decided once by the authority.
Mergeable writes MUST apply per column without waiting for other writes: concurrent writes to different columns both survive, and a later accepted write to the same column wins by arrival.
A row image MUST carry its deleted flag, so a replica can tell a deleted row from one it was never sent, including for rows it cached from an ended read.
A replica's synced result MUST equal the authority's read of the same query for that reader after any interleaving of writes, entering and leaving rows included.
Wire messages MUST name nodes by UUID, authors by identity and schemas by version id; node-local codes (interned author codes, rowids) never leave their database.

A serving peer MUST reject a capability-gapped live subscription with `SyncMessage::SubscribeRejected` addressed to the requested `SubscriptionKey`; the rejected subscription MUST NOT become active, `Unsubscribe` for it is a no-op, and the connection MUST keep serving other subscriptions.
A fresh subscription MUST receive its whole result; only a resumed one, whose client held it settled through a seq, may be sent just the rows changed after that seq.
A resumed subscription served only its changes since the seq it held MUST leave the replica with the same rows as a fresh subscription to the same query.

A receiver that finds an update naming a held row whose body it no longer has MUST reopen that view without known state, and the serving peer MUST then resend every row of the view with its body under ordinary read policy. There is no per-version fetch: rows are identified by `(row, row_seq)` and resent whole. A second such update for the same view before it settles is a protocol error rather than a resend loop.

Per-session delivery state (which versions a peer holds, its subscriptions) MUST live only in the serving process and be released on disconnect; it is never persisted, and session churn does not grow the server.
Results MUST travel as rows and be assembled into result trees by the receiver: no result-tree operations or relation edges travel on the wire.

A replica MUST treat a subscription as settled only when its connected upstream has confirmed it with a settled seq; while the upstream is unanswered, offline, failing or detached the subscription stays held, and a node with no upstream settles locally.

A downstream subscription MUST synchronize canonical authored facts with their logical table, row, transaction, authored schema, branch/source, fate, and witness identity intact under a closure manifest whose epoch, per-class inventory, and digest prove exact completeness; a projected application/terminal row is never replicated truth.

invariant: A receiver MUST select history/current and branch-overlay winners in authored lineage before projection, decode every fact under its authored schema, project it through the ordered lineage into the binding read schema, and run local IVM to derive terminal output. It MUST NOT supplement that residual program from unrelated local history. Raw bytes MUST NOT be relabeled as another schema and peer sync MUST NOT introduce `ProjectedAppRow` or an equivalent carrier.

An opaque admission MUST be rejected if replayed across a different authority lineage/epoch, manifest, shape/binding/read view, reader/policy revision, branch/SnapshotRef, residual-program identity, protected output/source occurrence, or concrete content/deletion/witness version and layer.

A strict remote read uses only its fresh exact authority closure; a local-first read may additionally include eligible local pending inputs. invariant: The read protocol MUST be rows plus settlement: the server sends row images, unlists and evictions and a settled seq; the receiver installs them and derives every result locally with its own compiled queries. No result sets or completeness facts travel.
Rows MUST be shipped under the schema version the subscriber declared, renamed by the lenses between it and the stored tables, support rows and permission advice included.
A replica missing the chunks of a large value MUST request them and install the row only once its chunks are present; a writer pushes a value's new chunks before the commit that uses them.

A Remote read MUST NOT report rows the server's answer no longer lists: rows the replica caches but the answer leaves out (lost access, deletions) are left out of the settled result, while local reads keep them.

A server MUST process a session's messages in the order sent, so a read sent after a commit is served after that commit; only while the ingress limit holds writes back may a read, which writes no rows, be served ahead of them.
Applying a fate or a settled seq MUST NOT move a node's settled seq backward or lower a write's reached durability tier; a lost fate is recovered on resume rather than guessed.

Rows MUST travel as self-contained row images (table, id, branch key, seq, deleted flag, content, cells), and result membership is per row: a subscription never holds a transaction as a unit of membership.

A server MUST track per session which row versions the peer holds and ship each version at most once across all of that peer's subscriptions; a peer it has no record of receives every row its results need.

A receiver MUST reject a `ViewUpdate` that names a `peer_payload_inventory.complete_tx_payloads`, add, or remove transaction it lacks enough tx existence, row-version payload, complete-tx payload, or view-complete serializable payload coverage to resolve for that subscription view.
Randomized differential suites MUST run from fixed seeds so any failure replays exactly.

Node-core simulation must be deterministic: time, randomness, and delivery order are injected by drivers, and failure to replay bit-for-bit is a bug. This is a guidance/process anchor, not runtime conformance.
Every consistency claim gets randomized or racing coverage: maintained and synced results against one-shot reads, merge convergence, and serializable validation under racing commits.
The canonical Jazz gate set (appendix D.1) is local-only until CI closes the groove-only gap. This is a guidance/process anchor, not runtime conformance.

Structured-result maintained-vs-one-shot equivalence MUST use canonical `ResultTree` equality, including ordered roots/relations, values, identity, descendants, aggregate/group payloads, and null/hole/empty semantics; root-membership set equality is insufficient.
implementation: planned structured differential oracle and receiver/chunk property

invariant: Canonical-sync reconstruction coverage MUST prove that a receiver derives its terminal from an authored-schema witness closure rather than a replicated projected row, across manifest/epoch integrity, lineage, branch isolation, policies, relations, aggregate inputs, reconnect/repair, recovery, and deterministic fault injection.
A public commit tick MUST advance logical time exactly once and evaluate all durable nodes before evaluating or routing subscription notifications.
Inner join output deltas MUST multiply input delta weight by stored opposite-side weight and MUST subtract one copy of the same-tick left/right cross term.
Anti-join output deltas MUST represent the visibility diff of left records for keys whose left or right inputs changed.
Snapshot and shape hydration MUST rebuild arrangements with `ArrangementUpdateMode::Replace` rather than accumulating a snapshot over existing arrangement contents.

A `Persist` node MUST consolidate all same-tick deltas by durable key before writing storage. A unique persist target MAY replace a stored owner only when that owner's net weight is fully retracted in the same tick and MUST reject the write unless at most one positive owner remains; same-tick reads MUST see staged durable writes through the tick overlay.
Prepared-shape output routing MUST update per-binding materialized weights and MUST send each output delta only to active subscriptions whose `BindingKey` equals the projected output key.
A recursive positive incremental tick MUST emit each newly discovered recursive fact at weight `+1` at most once and MUST collapse duplicate derivations.

The reference implementation selects recompute for negative table deltas, cached recursive state with table deltas, empty unbound state, or unhydrated step arrangements. This trigger set is broader than the minimum necessary; the contractual result is the minimal diff required by INV-REC-8.
Recursive recompute and incremental recursion MUST reject non-positive recursive frontier facts instead of assigning bag-recursive semantics.
Fixpoint recursion MUST stop with `RecursiveIterationLimit` when the frontier remains non-empty after its safety `max_iters`; semantic depth bounds MUST truncate instead.
Hydrating or querying a graph MUST NOT perturb an existing subscription stream's future tick deltas.
A subscription MUST receive exactly one initial hydration `RecordDeltas` message, including an empty message for an empty result, before it receives future commit deltas.
Contextual recursive child state MUST NOT be persisted in `operator_states` after recursive recompute; retained child operator state outside `FrontierSource` context remains root-scoped.
Commit notifications MUST contain weighted result deltas only; unchanged matching rows and base-table changes outside the query result MUST NOT be reported.
Same-key operations in one `DatabaseBatch` MUST compute deltas against prior operations in that batch, not only against pre-batch storage, and table deltas MUST be consolidated before ticking.
`TickEvaluator` MUST NOT reuse node outputs across different scopes, ticks, or recursive sub-ticks; per-tick memoized outputs MUST be cleared after the tick.

An arrangement MUST be a typed, hash-consed graph node whose identity includes its record-producing input, key fields, and comparison semantics. Consumers MUST depend on that node explicitly, so graph reachability governs sharing and lifecycle; runtime state adds evaluation scope to the node identity.
A root-scope arrangement MUST be stamped with `SubTick { tick: current_tick, sub_tick: 0 }`; only context-dependent arrangements may use the recursive evaluator's nonzero `sub_tick`.
Arrangement state MUST NOT move backward in logical time; stale reads MUST fail instead of returning data for the wrong `Tick`/`SubTick`.
In accumulate mode, advancing an arrangement more than once at the same `SubTick` MUST be idempotent so shared state absorbs each tick delta only once.
A transaction's staged writes MUST NOT be visible to ordinary reads or subscriptions before it commits, and a rolled-back transaction leaves nothing.
A write's reached durability MUST only rise (local, then global), and a wait for a tier the node can never reach fails instead of hanging.

The authority MUST give accepted commits a strictly increasing commit seq, stored in the same SQLite transaction as their rows, before it sends any fate; after reopen it continues above the highest seq it stored.
Local durability MUST NOT imply upstream survival: a write held only locally waits for its global tier, is resent after a restart or reconnect, and is lost only if its local file is.
A serializable transaction MUST capture the newest commit seq this node holds as its snapshot; a read the replica cannot answer from it asks the authority for that same snapshot.
Serializable snapshot reads MUST stay stable after later commits and record what they read, deleted rows and absent rows included.
Reads inside a serializable transaction MUST observe that transaction's own staged writes.
The authority MUST refuse a serializable commit when a row it read has changed or been deleted since its snapshot, including reads made through a schema view whose names differ from the stored ones.
The authority MUST refuse a serializable commit when a row it read as absent has since become present.

The authority MUST refuse a serializable commit when re-running one of its predicate reads, as the transaction's identity, returns a different result than at the snapshot (a phantom entering, a row leaving), and accept it when unrelated writes leave the result unchanged.
Serializable read validation MUST re-run each recorded read with its own bindings, from the query the commit carries, under the schema version it was read with.
Committing on a replica MUST apply the transaction locally as pending, record its upload in the same SQLite transaction, and send it upstream as one Commit.

Serializable writes MUST be first-committer-wins: a write whose base version is no longer the row's current version conflicts, a blind write over an unchanged row is accepted, and a commit over the writer's own unsettled write is accepted.
Each accepted commit MUST update the current tables and append to the history tables in the same SQLite transaction, so every accepted version is in history at its seq.
A replica MUST make a commit's rows visible only once all of them have arrived (frames, chunks); an incomplete commit stays invisible.

Only the authority MUST decide fates. A relay (a worker serving tabs, a backend) stores a downstream commit as pending, forwards it upstream, and assigns no seq and shows it at no global tier until the authority's fate arrives; a relay without an upstream settles its tabs locally.
A transaction handle MUST name the same work wherever it runs, and MUST be terminal after commit or rollback: any later operation on it is refused.

A local commit MUST be one SQLite transaction: its rows, history and upload record land together or not at all, so same-tick reads see the whole commit, a storage failure rolls it back whole with its own error, and a reopen after a crash shows exactly the committed prefix.

Client-side mergeable mutation staging MAY validate structure, schema, locally required preimages, and transaction consistency, but MUST NOT reject from a local read- or write-policy evaluation. The fate authority alone issues the definitive authorization verdict from complete admitted policy inputs.
implementation: planned client staging / authority admission separation

invariant: A commit MUST reach the authority and be applied whole however the transport splits it; the authority decides all of its writes together or none.
A commit the authority already decided MUST be idempotent: a resent copy (after a restart between apply and acknowledgement) gets the recorded fate and is not applied again.

A server MUST hold every message of a session whose declared schema version it has not admitted, deciding none of its commits, until that version is admitted; a read it cannot serve is refused with the reason, and a local writer on an unpublished schema is refused.
coverage: partial: holding a commit until admission has no direct test

invariant: A write MUST carry the base version of the row it was made over. The authority orders writes by its own commit seq, never by writer clocks: a later accepted write overrides earlier ones whatever its clock, and a write is never refused because the writer's clock is behind.
A writer's clock MUST only stamp provenance: a clock ahead of the authority gains its write no precedence, and explicit timestamps reach the authority per write as metadata.

When the authority refuses a transaction, its effects MUST leave the originating node's local view as soon as the refusal arrives, the row reverting to the authority's version, while the node's other pending writes stay and settle by their own fates; a refusal never cascades to other transactions.

The originating node MUST report each refused transaction to the application with its reason, naming the transaction even when the tab that made it has closed; other nodes never receive refused writes.

A wire-protocol v6 `WireFrame`, its reassembled semantic channel message, each WebSocket frame batch, and each independently versioned v1 NAPI/WASM binding payload MUST be exactly one complete postcard value: malformed, unsupported, corrupt-compressed, fragmented, or trailing-byte input MUST be rejected at its owning boundary before it can acquire a second interpretation. `WireHello.authority.node` MUST use postcard's length-prefixed 16-byte `NodeUuid` representation and be consumed before the exact-frame EOF check. Frozen frame, Hello, semantic-payload, branch/catalogue/large-value, and binding corpus cases MUST decode independently and re-encode to their exact approved bytes.

Every wire tagged union is closed and strictly decoded within a wire version; additive variants, messages and error codes are emitted only behind a negotiated feature bit. Across wire versions only the `Hello` tag plus `min_protocol_version`/`max_protocol_version` prefix and the complete `Error` frame with its baseline codes and retries are shared: a receiver MUST read a Hello's version range before its version-scoped body and answer a foreign range with `UnsupportedProtocolVersion`/`Never`, never `MalformedFrame`.
